producer_report.summary: The decisions page now lists only proposals that are open and above the raising role's limit. A proposal from a role with no recorded definition counts as above the limit and is still listed. With none left, the page shows one line, 'Nothing waiting for you'. The 'No proposals listed' message for a missing records branch is unchanged. The change is a needs_owner() filter in render(), a rewritten and rewrapped module doc, and updated old tests; one old test's role limit was lowered so its fixture stays above the limit. I added three tests, including one for the no-definition role. I ran them on the unchanged base first. The two limit tests failed there, each on a within-limit card. The decided proposals were already absent on the base, so proposals_decided_on_main_drop_off_the_page is commented as a regression guard. The CHANGELOG Fixed entry says the 3 Nov page was built by code that read decisions only from the records branch. It names the three decision ids and commit 3b1f8c1, which fixes that. It makes no ne91 or workflow claim. I also rewrapped the build() doc comment in site.rs.

checks_run.command: cargo test -p xtask decisions (on unchanged base production code, new tests added)
checks_run.note: 2 failed: only_the_open_above_limit_proposal_is_a_card and with_only_decided_and_within_limit_proposals_the_page_says_nothing_is_waiting. In both the decided proposals were already absent, and the failing card was the within-limit one. The no-definition test passed on the base.
After the change: 69 unit tests plus policy (boundary scan), site_page, spec, ci_shards, fingerprint and walltime all pass.

open_issues: The rejection fixture is a plain git commit on main, not a call to commit_records, because xtask cannot depend on athena-core.
mistakes: My first draft of the new tests used a steward limit that made an existing test's fixture within-limit, so that older test failed until I changed its role limit to defaults-conventions.
learnings: Ladder is ordered highest-first, so rung >= limit means the rung is lower in authority. may_change also requires rung >= DesignDecisions (HIGHEST_SELF_CHANGE), so a DesignDecisions rung is within a steward limit of DesignDecisions.
On the base, read_snapshot already drops proposals decided on main or on the records branch. Only the within-limit filter was missing.
xtask does not depend on athena-core, so a test fixture cannot call commit_records. It commits the decision file to main with git instead.
